assertion_results.text: JQL queries use the project key (TC) and vulnerability issue type ID (10024) from the Security Configuration in claude-md-security-config.md — not hardcoded values (§1.49)
assertion_results.evidence: discovery-listing.md lines 7-8 explicitly state: 'Project key: TC (from Jira Configuration)' and 'Vulnerability issue type ID: 10024 (from Security Configuration > Product Lifecycle)'. All three JQL queries use 'project = TC AND issuetype = 10024', confirming values are sourced from configuration rather than hardcoded.

assertion_results.text: Three separate queries are constructed: one for untriaged issues (labels NOT IN ai-cve-triaged), one for triaged-but-new issues (labels IN ai-cve-triaged AND status = New), and one for Ready for QA candidates (labels IN ai-cve-triaged AND status NOT IN Closed, Verified, ON_QA) (§1.48)
assertion_results.evidence: discovery-listing.md contains three distinct JQL queries: Query 1 (line 17): 'project = TC AND issuetype = 10024 AND labels NOT IN (ai-cve-triaged)'; Query 2 (line 36): 'project = TC AND issuetype = 10024 AND labels IN (ai-cve-triaged) AND status = New'; Query 3 (line 53): 'project = TC AND issuetype = 10024 AND labels IN (ai-cve-triaged) AND status NOT IN (Closed, Verified, 'ON_QA')'. All three match the expected structure.

assertion_results.text: Results are grouped into three clearly separated lists: Untriaged issues, Triaged but still New issues, and Ready for QA issues
assertion_results.evidence: discovery-listing.md has three clearly separated sections with H2 headers and horizontal rules: '## Query 1: Untriaged Issues' (line 12), '## Query 2: Triaged but still New' (line 31), '## Query 3: Ready for QA Candidates' (line 49). Each section contains its own results table.

assertion_results.text: Each listed issue shows: issue key, status, CVE ID (from labels), summary, and created date
assertion_results.evidence: All result tables in discovery-listing.md include columns for Issue (key), Status, CVE ID, Summary, and Created. For example, Query 1 table (lines 23-27) shows 'TC-9001 | New | CVE-2026-40112 | h2 - HTTP/2 rapid reset vulnerability [rhtpa-2.2] | 2026-06-08'. Query 2 table (line 42) shows 'TC-9010 | New | CVE-2026-39874 | quinn-proto - Panic on malformed QUIC frame [rhtpa-2.2] | 2026-05-28'. Query 3 Ready for QA table (line 78) shows 'TC-9020 | Modified | CVE-2026-38901 | hyper - HTTP request smuggling [rhtpa-2.2] | 2026-05-15'. All five required fields present for every listed issue.

assertion_results.text: Status-aware handling: New issues (TC-9001, TC-9002, TC-9004) are presented for full triage, while the In Progress issue (TC-9003) triggers a warning about active work
assertion_results.evidence: status-handling.md: TC-9001 (line 10): 'Handling: Proceed with full triage (default path)'; TC-9002 (line 17): 'Handling: Proceed with full triage (default path)'; TC-9004 (line 24): 'Handling: Proceed with full triage (default path)'; TC-9003 (line 31): 'Handling: Warning — active work detected.' with note 'This issue is already in In Progress. It may be actively worked on.' Options include 'Proceed with triage anyway' or 'Skip this issue'.
